title: The Crow and the Pitcher
source: Aesop's Fables, tr. G. F. Townsend (1867), 'The Crow and the Pitcher'
lesson: Little by little does the trick.
lines: It was the hottest day of the year. The streams had dried up, and a crow was dying of thirst.
Then he spotted a pitcher! He flew down with delight, and peeked inside. There was water, but only a little, right at the bottom.
He pushed his beak in as far as it would go. Too short. He tried to tip the pitcher over. Too heavy.
Then he had an idea. He picked up a small stone, and dropped it in. Plop.
Then another. And another. Plop. Plop. Plop. Slowly, very slowly, the water began to rise.
Stone by stone, it came up, until at last it reached his beak. He drank, and drank, and saved his life.
Little by little does the trick. When a problem looks too big, don't give up. Drop one small stone at a time.
Next episode: a donkey who wanted to sing like a grasshopper. Follow so you don't miss it!
